title: Retail Management
overview: Successful retail management requires the coordinated management of customers, people, merchandise, operations, inventory, sales performance, and the overall store experience. Retail managers must achieve commercial targets while maintaining service standards, operational discipline, product availability, employee productivity, and a consistent brand experience.

This three-day course provides retail managers and supervisors with a practical framework for managing store performance. Participants examine retail strategy, customer behavior, store operations, merchandise and inventory control, visual merchandising, sales conversion, service quality, team leadership, scheduling, loss prevention, retail KPIs, and performance improvement.

Through retail cases, store-performance exercises, KPI analysis, merchandising scenarios, customer-service situations, staffing activities, and action planning, participants learn how to manage the retail environment systematically and improve both customer experience and commercial results.
audience: Retail managers, store managers, assistant store managers, retail supervisors, department managers, area and branch managers, retail operations professionals, sales supervisors, merchandising professionals, and employees preparing for retail-management responsibilities.
methodology: The course uses an applied methodology combining short presentations, retail-management cases, store-performance analysis, customer-journey exercises, merchandise and inventory scenarios, visual-merchandising activities, staffing and scheduling exercises, sales and service simulations, KPI analysis, loss-prevention cases, group discussion, and individual action planning.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Explain the key responsibilities and commercial priorities of effective retail management.
Analyze customer behavior and manage the store experience around customer needs.
Organize store operations to maintain efficiency, consistency, and service quality.
Manage merchandise availability, inventory levels, replenishment, and stock accuracy.
Apply visual-merchandising principles to support customer navigation and sales.
Improve sales conversion, average transaction value, and complementary selling.
Lead, schedule, coach, and motivate retail employees effectively.
Use retail KPIs to diagnose performance and identify improvement priorities.
Manage complaints and service-recovery situations professionally.
Reduce operational losses through disciplined controls and loss-prevention practices.
Plan promotional and peak-period execution effectively.
Develop a practical action plan for improving store performance.
